question.question:
D1 — Is this a Library/SDK plan delivered as Documentation?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-Dt51ml on main, reviewing PLAN.md "SDK quickstart docs".
ELI10: The plan describes 8 steps a developer follows before making a first SDK call, and it is titled as quickstart docs. How I classify it decides which personas I offer next and which parts of the journey I weigh most (install and hello-world for an SDK, findability and copy-paste code for docs). The stakes: pick the wrong lens and I score the wrong things.
Stakes if we pick wrong: I'd benchmark against the wrong peers and offer personas that don't match your actual reader.
Recommendation: A because the plan's only artifact is a docs flow whose endpoint is "make your first SDK call" — it is docs about an SDK, both lenses apply, SDK is primary.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: choosing the lens, not the scope; nothing about the plan changes yet.

options.label: SDK + Docs (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Matches the plan's endpoint (first SDK call) and its title (quickstart docs), so TTHW and copy-paste code both get weighed ✅ Lets me benchmark against SDK onboarding peers (Stripe, Twilio, Supabase) which is where the 8-step flow will be judged ❌ Treats the dev server and Postgres steps as SDK install friction, which may overweight them if this is really a self-hosted platform

options.label: Platform (self-hosted)
options.description: ✅ Steps 3-5 (env vars, migrations, dev server) read like standing up a self-hosted service, which is a platform journey ✅ Benchmarks shift to Supabase self-host / Appwrite / PocketBase, which is fairer if devs must run the backend ❌ Deemphasizes the SDK call and curl example the plan itself names as the goal

options.label: Documentation only
options.description: ✅ Scores the docs artifact on its own terms: findability, structure, copy-paste code, context switching ✅ Avoids recommending product changes the docs team cannot make ❌ Ignores that half the friction (email for API key, 8 env vars) is product, not prose, and a docs-only lens would let it slide

question.question:
D1 — Product type: is this primarily a Documentation plan (SDK quickstart) for an SDK backed by a key-gated API?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-Bd5h1O on main, reviewing PLAN.md "SDK quickstart docs".
ELI10: The review calibrates against different gold standards depending on what the developer is actually touching. A docs plan gets judged on whether the words get someone to a working call fast; an SDK plan gets judged on install and API shape; an API plan on curl and key issuance. The plan title says docs, but steps 3-5 and 7 are infra and key-issuance work, so the classification is not obvious.
Stakes if we pick wrong: I benchmark against the wrong peers and score dimensions that don't apply, and the friction trace misses the stage where developers actually leave.
Recommendation: A because the plan's deliverable is the quickstart guide; the SDK and API are the things it documents, not what it changes.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: pick the surface the plan changes, and I'll still hold the SDK and API constraints fixed as context.

options.label: Documentation (primary) (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Matches the plan title and the 3 declared gaps (quickstart cmd, sandbox, curl), all docs-adjacent. ✅ Lets the review judge words and step count against docs peers like Stripe/Supabase quickstarts. ❌ Treats the local dev server and key-by-email as fixed constraints, so fixes are limited to how they're documented and sequenced.

options.label: Library/SDK (primary)
options.description: ✅ Puts install, import, and first-call ergonomics at the center of scoring. ✅ Benchmarks against SDK peers (Stripe SDKs, Supabase client) on time to first call. ❌ The plan doesn't change SDK code, so most findings would land outside the plan's scope.

options.label: API/Service (primary)
options.description: ✅ Centers key issuance and the missing curl example, which are the largest declared gaps. ✅ Benchmarks the email-for-a-key step against self-serve dashboards. ❌ The plan can't change the key-issuance process itself in DX POLISH mode; only how it's documented.

options.label: Platform (local stack + docs)
options.description: ✅ Treats Postgres, migrations, env vars, and dev server as the real onboarding surface. ✅ Benchmarks against docker-compose / devcontainer style starts. ❌ Reframes a docs plan as an infra plan, which crosses the scope the user asked me to preserve.
